questions.question_text: Headquarters of Indian Railways is in:
questions.explanation: Indian Railways is a ministry-level organization under the Government of India, and all major central government ministries and their headquarters are located in Delhi, the national capital, where administrative control and policy decisions are centralized.

questions.question_text: First Railway in India ran between:
questions.explanation: India's first railway line, opened on April 16, 1853, connected Bombay (Mumbai) to Thane, covering approximately 34 km. This historic route preceded other major railway connections and marked the beginning of India's railway era.
Japan's official currency is the Yen (JPY). Yuan is China's currency, Won is used in Korea, and Rupee is India's currency.

The Antarctic Desert is the largest desert by area at approximately 14 million square kilometers, covering the entire Antarctic continent. While the Sahara is the largest hot desert, deserts are defined by precipitation levels, not temperature, making Antarctica technically the world's largest desert.

Pratibha Patil served as India's President from 2007 to 2012, making her the first woman to hold this constitutional position. Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister, not President, while Sonia Gandhi and Sushma Swaraj never held the presidential office.

questions.question_text: Constitution of India came into effect on:
questions.explanation: The Constitution was drafted by the Constituent Assembly and adopted on November 26, 1949, but came into effect on January 26, 1950, which is celebrated as Republic Day in India.

Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' during his imprisonment in 1944-1945. It's a historical and philosophical work exploring India's civilization, culture, and path to independence, reflecting Nehru's intellectual perspective on the nation's identity.

The Lotus was declared India's national flower because it holds profound significance in Indian culture, philosophy, and religion, particularly in Hinduism and Buddhism, symbolizing purity and enlightenment. It also appears on the national emblem and currency.

ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation) was established in 1969 and has been headquartered in Bengaluru since its inception. The city hosts ISRO's main administrative office and several key research facilities.

Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is called the Father of the Indian Constitution because he chaired the Drafting Committee that prepared the Constitution and played the pivotal role in shaping its fundamental structure and principles.

Kanchenjunga (28,169 feet) is the highest mountain peak entirely within Indian territory. While Mount Everest is taller globally, it lies on the India-Nepal border. K2 and Nanda Devi are lower peaks in the Himalayas.

The speed of light in vacuum is approximately 300,000 km/s or 300,000,000 m/s, which equals 3×10⁸ m/s. The other options represent incorrect powers of 10 that would be far too slow (A, C) or too fast (D).

Dadasaheb Phalke is called the "Father of Indian Cinema" because he directed the first full-length Indian feature film "Raja Harishchandra" in 1913, pioneering the Indian film industry and establishing cinema as a major medium in India.

The Bhakra-Nangal Dam is constructed on the Sutlej River in Punjab. It's one of India's oldest and most significant multipurpose dams, built across the Sutlej as it flows through the Himalayas before descending into the plains.

India has 28 states after Telangana was formed as the 29th state in 2014, but this question reflects the count of 28 states, which was accurate until Jammu and Kashmir's reorganization in 2019 reduced the number of states to 27 (with J&K becoming a union territory). However, option A (28) represents the standard constitutional answer for most reference materials of that period.

questions.question_text: World Environment Day is observed on:
questions.explanation: World Environment Day is celebrated on June 5th each year, commemorating the opening of the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment held in Stockholm on that date in 1972.

Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise capital city between the rival cities of Sydney and Melbourne, and was officially established as Australia's capital in 1927. Though Sydney is the most populous city, it is not the capital.

questions.question_text: Light Year is a unit of:
questions.explanation: A light year measures the distance that light travels through vacuum in one year, approximately 9.46 trillion kilometers. Despite containing the word "year" (a time unit), it quantifies spatial distance, not time.

Diamond is a crystalline form of carbon where each carbon atom bonds to four other carbon atoms in an extremely hard tetrahedral structure. Allotropes are different physical forms of the same element, making carbon the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Brain is part of which system?
questions.explanation: The brain is the control center of the body and is the primary organ of the nervous system, which processes sensory information and controls bodily functions through electrical and chemical signals.

questions.question_text: PM CARES Fund was set up in:
questions.explanation: The PM CARES Fund was established on March 28, 2020, in response to the COVID-19 pandemic to provide relief and support for affected individuals and communities across India.

Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award of India, established in 1954 to honor exceptional service in any field of human endeavor. The Padma awards (Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri) rank below it in the civilian honors hierarchy.

The ozone layer absorbs ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun, particularly UV-B and UV-C rays, preventing them from reaching Earth's surface where they would cause skin cancer, cataracts, and immune suppression in living organisms.

Common cold is caused by viruses, most commonly rhinoviruses. Bacteria, fungi, and protozoa cause different types of infections but not the common cold, which is a viral respiratory illness characterized by inflammation of the upper respiratory tract.

Kalpana Chawla was the first woman of Indian origin to go to space in 1997 aboard Space Shuttle Columbia. While Sunita Williams is also of Indian descent and has spent more time in space, Kalpana Chawla achieved the milestone first chronologically.
